questions: Should the random seed be set inside the function to ensure reproducibility across calls, or should the function rely on external seeding?
Are the items in the shopping cart meant to be selected uniformly at random from POSSIBLE_ITEMS, or can any distribution be used as long as frequencies match lengths?
Should the function handle cases where list_of_lists contains non-list elements (e.g., tuples or other iterables), or only strict lists?
Is the order of the returned list of Counters required to match the order of the input list_of_lists exactly?
Should the Counter objects include only items from POSSIBLE_ITEMS, or can they contain other keys if POSSIBLE_ITEMS is modified externally?
If a sublist has length zero, is the corresponding Counter required to be empty, or could it contain items with zero counts?
Should the function ensure that the total count in each Counter equals the length of the corresponding sublist, even if random selections produce duplicates?
Is the function allowed to have side effects, such as modifying the input list_of_lists or global state?
